name: Banakil
description: Banakil is a popular Rummy-style game widely played in Jordan, Palestine, Syria, and Lebanon. The name is derived from 'Bankal', the Arabic term for a 'Wild Two'. Using two full decks and distinct wild card rules, Banakil features a high initial hand size (18 cards) and a counter-clockwise play direction. It is a game of meticulous organization, where players must balance the pursuit of high-value melds against the risk of holding unmatched cards if an opponent suddenly 'goes out'.

content.text: Banakil is a popular Rummy-style game widely played in Jordan, Palestine, Syria, and Lebanon. The name is derived from 'Bankal', the Arabic term for a 'Wild Two'. Using two full decks and distinct wild card rules, Banakil features a high initial hand size (18 cards) and a counter-clockwise play direction. It is a game of meticulous organization, where players must balance the pursuit of high-value melds against the risk of holding unmatched cards if an opponent suddenly 'goes out'.

Developed in the Levant as a regional adaptation of mid-20th century European Rummy games. It distinguished itself by incorporating all 2s as wild cards (the namesake 'Banakil'), echoing the mechanics of Canasta but within a purer Rummy framework.
2-4 players. (4 players usually play in partners; 2-3 play individually).
Standard pack, score sheet, non-transparent discard tray.
Dealer (rotating counter-clockwise) deals 18 cards to each player. The next card is placed face up on the table (The Ground) to start the discard pile. The rest is the Stock.

items.text: Partnership Banakil: Partners can add to each other's melds after their own initial meld is on the table.
